task_objective: Build the backup-to-recovery timeline and distinguish a missing later file state from an unexplained whole-file absence.

rius.description: Report that the backup completed at midnight.

scoring_rule.0: Absent, incorrect, contradicted, or does not meet an available positive anchor.
scoring_rule.1: Report that the backup completed at midnight.

rius.rationale: The backup boundary is central to the timeline and to whether the later modification could be included.

rius.description: Report that a file was modified at 12:15 AM.

scoring_rule.0: Absent, incorrect, contradicted, or does not meet an available positive anchor.
scoring_rule.1: Report that a file was modified at 12:15 AM.

rius.rationale: This is the post-backup change whose recovery is in question.

rius.description: Report that the system failed at 12:30 AM.

scoring_rule.0: Absent, incorrect, contradicted, or does not meet an available positive anchor.
scoring_rule.1: Report that the system failed at 12:30 AM.

rius.rationale: Preserves the failure time; the coverage/absence distinction can remain sound without this exact timed event.

rius.description: Report that restore began at 1:00 AM.

scoring_rule.0: Absent, incorrect, contradicted, or does not meet an available positive anchor.
scoring_rule.1: Report that restore began at 1:00 AM.

rius.rationale: Preserves restore timing without implying completion at that time; the selected restore point matters separately.

rius.description: State that the restore used the midnight backup.

scoring_rule.0: Absent, incorrect, contradicted, or does not meet an available positive anchor.
scoring_rule.1: State that the restore used the midnight backup.

rius.rationale: Without the selected restore point the missing post-backup state cannot be interpreted.

rius.description: Report that the modified file was not present after recovery, as stated, without silently replacing this observation with a different confirmed outcome.

scoring_rule.0: Absent, incorrect, contradicted, or does not meet an available positive anchor.
scoring_rule.1: Report that the modified file was not present after recovery, as stated, without silently replacing this observation with a different confirmed outcome.

rius.rationale: The observed absence is the ambiguity the explanation must address.

rius.description: Present the events in order: midnight backup completion, 12:15 AM file modification, 12:30 AM system failure, then the 1:00 AM restore start and subsequent recovery observation.

scoring_rule.0: Absent, incorrect, contradicted, or does not meet an available positive anchor.
scoring_rule.1: Present the events in order: midnight backup completion, 12:15 AM file modification, 12:30 AM system failure, then the 1:00 AM restore start and subsequent recovery observation.

rius.rationale: Without ordering the supplied events the response does not build the requested timeline.

rius.description: Explain that the 12:15 AM modification is later than the completed midnight backup, so restoring that backup would not normally restore the later modification.

scoring_rule.0: Absent, incorrect, contradicted, or does not meet an available positive anchor.
scoring_rule.1: Explain that the 12:15 AM modification is later than the completed midnight backup, so restoring that backup would not normally restore the later modification.

rius.rationale: Without the backup-coverage relationship the answer misses the principal defensible explanation for loss of the later state.

rius.description: Explain that the timeline alone does not establish why the entire file would be absent rather than only its later state missing; whether the file was included in the backup or what the restore recovered remains to be established.

scoring_rule.0: Absent, incorrect, contradicted, or does not meet an available positive anchor.
scoring_rule.1: Explain that the timeline alone does not establish why the entire file would be absent rather than only its later state missing; whether the file was included in the backup or what the restore recovered remains to be established.

rius.rationale: Treating an out-of-backup modification as proof of whole-file absence resolves an ambiguity the evidence does not settle.

notes: E4 draft; frozen prompt corpus v0.3.1, protocol 0.3, annotation schema 0.2. EN/BN/BN-CS interpretation: All variants retain midnight backup completion, 12:15 AM modification, 12:30 AM failure, 1 AM restore from the midnight backup and nonpresence of the modified file after recovery. The ambiguity about file versus later version is shared. Boundaries: Four event-time relations, selected restore point, recovery observation, ordering, backup coverage and residual ambiguity are distinct. No file creation time, backup membership, later backup, restore success for every other file or exact loss mechanism is supplied. Timing can explain the missing later change but is not proof that an earlier existing file should vanish. Equivalent wording, scripts and numerals are accepted.
